title: NEUROTOKEN: Joint Source and Directional AAD with Envelope Decoding via Conditional Flow Matching
abstract: arXiv:2610.00397v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Identifying which speaker a listener is attending to in a noisy room -- the cocktail-party problem -- is the missing ingredient for next-generation hearing aids and brain-computer interfaces: it tells the device whose voice to amplify. Auditory attention decoding (AAD) reads this answer from EEG, but the literature splits into disconnected pieces: directional-AAD classifies side but does not map side to stream; regression-based source-AAD ranks candidate streams by a single Pearson correlation that is intrinsically noisy at the 1-5 s windows real devices need; and envelope reconstruction has no native AAD rule. We argue the right object is not any single statistic but the conditional likelihood of the attended envelope given EEG, and we make this practical with NEUROTOKEN: a single network whose three heads share one EEG front-end, with a conditional flow-matching head (ATTUNEFLOW) that scores candidates by an integrated velocity-residua

translated_title: NEUROTOKEN：通过条件流匹配包络解码实现声源与方向的联合听觉注意力解码（AAD）
translated_abstract: 在嘈杂环境中识别听者正在关注哪位说话者——即“鸡尾酒会问题”——是下一代助听器与脑机接口所缺失的关键一环：它告诉设备应该放大谁的声音。听觉注意力解码（AAD）从脑电（EEG）中读取这一答案，但现有文献被割裂为互不相关的几个分支：方向性AAD只能判断声音来自哪一侧，却无法将方位映射到具体的语音流；基于回归的声源AAD依赖单一皮尔逊相关系数对候选语音流进行排序，而这种指标在真实设备所需的1-5秒时间窗内天然噪声较大；包络重建方法则缺乏原生的AAD判别规则。本文认为，正确的建模对象不应是任何单一统计量，而应是给定EEG条件下被关注包络的条件似然，并通过NEUROTOKEN使其成为现实：这是一个三输出头共享同一EEG前端的单一网络，其中的条件流匹配头（ATTUNEFLOW）通过积分速度残差对候选包络进行打分……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: NEUROTOKEN用一个三输出头共享EEG前端的单一网络，将声源级与方向性听觉注意力解码及包络重建统一到同一框架中，并通过条件流匹配头计算被关注语音包络在给定EEG下的条件似然，从而在真实设备所需的1-5秒短时窗内实现更可靠的“鸡尾酒会问题”解码。
en_tdlr: NEUROTOKEN unifies source-level and directional auditory attention decoding with envelope reconstruction in a single three-head network sharing one EEG front-end, using a conditional flow-matching head (AttuneFlow) to score candidate speech envelopes by their conditional likelihood given EEG, enabling robust short-window (1-5 s) cocktail-party decoding for real-world hearing aids and brain-computer interfaces.
